title: Bash example uses the '!`cmd`' pattern, which executes on skill load instead of displaying as an example
body: The fenced bash block shows `!`git status`` under 'Check the working tree before releasing:', which reads as illustrative sample text. But the SKILL.md parser executes '!' backtick patterns even inside fenced code blocks (this is the documented GitHub #12781 bug the project's own CLAUDE.md/skill-development.md rules warn about). So this is not an inert example a reader can safely copy or read past -- it actually runs 'git status' the moment the skill is loaded, silently, with no indication to the reader that the block is live code rather than documentation. A reader trusting this as a shown example is misled about what the file does. Fix: use '$ git status' notation (as the project's own anti-pattern rule prescribes) so the block renders as inert text.
